newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Powerful Cambodian PM says no need to stage coup.
newsitem.headline: Powerful Cambodian PM says no need to stage coup.

text.p: Cambodian strongman Hun Sen said on Monday there was no need for him to stage a coup because he already had enough power.

The second prime minister, in a speech aired on the radio station of his Cambodian People's Party (CPP), said he had told foreign ambassadors: "If I stage a coup now, there is no one who could stop me."
Hun Sen explained that the main commanders in the police and armed forces were his proteges and far from retirement age.
"Why should I make a coup? The purpose of making a coup is to take what we don't yet have. It is only the people with no power who stage a coup to take power," he said.
Hun Sen, speaking at a pagoda ground-breaking ceremony, said he was recognised inside and outside Cambodia as a legitimate ruler. "So why do I need to make an illegal coup to take illegal power?"
The remarks were an apparent swipe at the role of co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranarridh, who shares power with Hun Sen in a shaky coalition formed following U.N.-sponsored polls in 1993.

The two leaders have feuded over power-sharing issues for months, and relations have deteriorated since a deadly March 30 grenade attack on a demonstration led by opposition leader and Ranariddh ally, Sam Rainsy.
The relationship plummeted further two weeks ago, when Hun Sen supported royal dissidents who had broken with Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party.
Meanwhile, Rainsy, who was due to return to Phnom Penh on Monday, has delayed his return until next month, officials from FUNCINPEC told Reuters.
Parliamentarian and human rights committee chief Kem Sokha told Reuters he had asked Sam Rainsy to stay in Europe because of security concerns.
